hist_down1.png: Histogram of 2,261 NHL goalie pulls while trailing by one, on a game clock from 7:00 to 0:00. The model's best window, 4:13 to 3:13 left, is shaded and nearly empty; the typical pull comes at 1:57, 1:45 after the best time of 3:42. 29 pulls (1.3%) came within 10 seconds of the best time, or earlier. The last bar on the left holds every pull at 6:45 or earlier.
hist_down2.png: Histogram of 1,524 NHL goalie pulls while trailing by two, on a game clock from 10:00 to 0:00. The model's best window, 7:55 to 5:05 left, is shaded and nearly empty; the typical pull comes at 3:03, 3:18 after the best time of 6:21. 16 pulls (1.0%) came within 10 seconds of the best time, or earlier. The last bar on the left holds every pull at 9:45 or earlier.
curve_down1.png: U-shaped curve of standings points lost per 100 games by goalie pull time when trailing by one with 10:00 left, with a 90% uncertainty band. The minimum is at 3:42 left (90% range 4:13 to 3:13). The NHL median pull at 1:57 costs about 1.4 points per 100 games.
curve_down2.png: U-shaped curve of standings points lost per 100 games by goalie pull time when trailing by two with 10:00 left, with a 90% uncertainty band. The minimum is at 6:21 left (90% range 7:55 to 5:05). The NHL median pull at 3:03 costs about 0.6 points per 100 games.
cost_curves.png: Two stacked curves of standings points lost per 100 games by pull time. Down one the best time is 3:42 and the NHL median 1:57 costs 1.4 points per 100 games. Down two the best time is 6:21 and the median 3:03 costs 0.6. Both carry 90% bands.
trend.png: Line chart of the NHL median goalie pull time by season from 2021-22 to 2026-27. Down one it moved from 1:54 to 2:03 against a best time of 3:42; down two from 2:56 to 3:04 against 6:21. The last season is partial.
buckets_down1.png: Dot plot of the share of teams trailing by one with 3:00 left that tied or won, grouped by when the goalie came out, with 95% ranges, against the model's expectation. 2:30 to 3:00: 20% real, 18% model, n=311. 2:00 to 2:29: 21% real, 18% model, n=727. 1:30 to 1:59: 20% real, 17% model, n=683. 1:00 to 1:29: 10% real, 16% model, n=277. under 1:00 or never: 6% real, 13% model, n=143.
buckets_down2.png: Dot plot of the share of teams trailing by two with 5:00 left that tied or won, grouped by when the goalie came out, with 95% ranges, against the model's expectation. 4:00 to 5:00: 3.2% real, 4.0% model, n=190. 3:00 to 3:59: 4.3% real, 3.8% model, n=510. 2:00 to 2:59: 4.3% real, 3.5% model, n=486. under 2:00 or never: 1.2% real, 2.4% model, n=258.
calibration.png: Calibration plot of predicted against observed chance of getting at least a point, 10 bins with 95% ranges, all close to the diagonal from 0.02 to 0.31. Fit on 2021-22 to 2024-25, tested on 2025-26 and 2026-27. Predicted 17.3%, observed 18.2%. Brier 0.1385 against a baseline of 0.1391; AUC 0.690 against 0.685.
teams.png: Horizontal bar chart ranking all 32 NHL teams by standings points lost to late goalie pulls per 82 games, 2024-25 to 2026-27. WPG loses the most at 0.58, DAL the least at 0.20; the league average is 0.38.
sensitivity.png: Dot plot of the best goalie pull time in the main case and 7 alternative assumptions. Down one it stays between 3:23 and 4:13; down two between 5:28 and 7:05. Cases: Main: all seasons, standings points, OT 50/50: 3:42 and 6:21; Playoff mode: win probability: 3:58 and 6:35; Overtime win rate 45 percent for the team that came back: 3:43 and 6:22; Overtime win rate 55 percent: 3:41 and 6:20; Train seasons only (2021-22 to 2024-25): 3:23 and 7:05; Trailing 5 on 5 rates from the whole third period: 3:50 and 6:25; All manpower states (penalties folded in): 3:39 and 6:55; Recent seasons only (2024-25 onward): 4:13 and 5:28.
rates.png: Two dumbbell charts of third-period goals scored and allowed per 60 minutes with the goalie in net versus pulled, for teams trailing by one, two and three. Down 1: scored 2.5 to 6.9, allowed 2.1 to 20.3. Down 2: scored 2.6 to 6.7, allowed 2.5 to 23.5. Down 3: scored 2.2 to 8.5, allowed 2.4 to 21.2.
